main_text.p: §. 20. Et removit rotas curruum &c. v. 25. verbum ויסר à סור recedere, quod in hiph. est removere. LXX. deduxe-runt ab אסר ligare, unde reddunt; καὶ συνέδησε τὰς ἀξονας τῆς ἁρμάτων αὐτῶν. Καὶ ἤγαγεν αὐτὰς μετὰ βίας. Ligavit axes currum eorum, & egit eos cum violentia. In Hebr. בכבד cum pondere, i. e. tardè, impedite, vel ut Paraphr. Jon. בקשין difficulter. Itaque Deus Ægyptios hac tarditate detinebat in via, populo interim Isr. ad salutis portum contendente, priusquam hostium internecionem faceret. Sic illaqueato hosti, ut non posset effugere, vindictæ divinæ prodigia hanc invito confessionem extorsere: fugiam à facie Israëlis, quia Jehova pugnat pro eis. Hic iterum fabulandi locum invenerunt Rabini. Targum Hierof. ad verba; & removit rotas, &c. הון מרכרין להון גרירן מן בתריהון אורחהון דמולותא (lege דמולותא) מהווין נגדן לגלגליא חזרו גלגליא וירידותא למיהוין נגדן למוליתא ורמין על ימא Ducebant (currus) tractos post se: mos mularum erat trahere rotas: at vice versa rotæ & currus mulas trahebant & projiciebant in mare? Papæ! R. Abrah: in Zeror Hammor, ad eadem verba; כי מכח האש נשרפו הגלגליים לפי שהיו וכו' Quia vi ignis comburebantur rotæ quippe lignea: hinc reperimus Siseram inde cautiorem factum accepisse noningentos currus ferreos, ne ignis vi sua in eos dominari posset. Jud. 4. 13. Dignæ fabulæ, quæ addantur veris narrationibus Luciani. Putidiora habent in Medrafchim, quæ referre pudor prohibet.

§. 21. Videamus jam paucis ipsam, quæ supereft, Tragœdiæ Ægyptiorum catastrophen. page.notes: Hebrew and Greek lines are copied from the scan and are not checked against a source; the Rabbinic lines (Targum, Abrah. Zeror Hammor) are the least certain and may contain errors, including the "(lege ...)" correction, which is read as printed. The Greek "τῆς ἁρμάτων" is read as printed. A faint mark at the foot centre (possible gathering signature) is too indistinct to record and is left out. The "§. 20" line at the top is an italic lemma inside the text, not a heading.
